candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — transmission-based precautions
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — Droplet Precautions
candidate.educational_objective: Apply the core PPE requirement for Droplet Precautions at room entry.

options.A: Enter without facial PPE unless an aerosol-generating procedure is planned
options.B: Use a fit-tested N95 respirator for routine droplet care because a medical mask is inadequate
options.C: Require a negative-pressure airborne infection isolation room for all droplet infections
options.D: Don a mask upon entry into the patient room or patient space

candidate.rationale: CDC Transmission-Based Precautions guidance states that healthcare personnel should use PPE appropriately for Droplet Precautions and don a mask upon entry into the patient room or patient space. Routine Droplet Precautions do not require special air handling or a negative-pressure room. D is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: For Droplet Precautions, healthcare personnel don a mask upon entry; special air handling/ventilation is not required for routine droplet transmission.
candidate.source_locator: Droplet Precautions section — use PPE appropriately; don mask upon entry into patient room or patient space
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
candidate.stem: A client requires Droplet Precautions. Which action should the nurse take when entering the client's room or patient space?
